titulo: Observability: logging calls, errors, and cancellations
lead: In production, "the agent couldn't book" only gets solved with a log. Every tool call, through any door, leaves a line: surface, tool, result, and time. No personal data. In this lesson you trigger the possible outcomes and read what each one leaves in the log.
objetivo: log every call across the three surfaces with result and time, with no personal data, and read the possible outcomes in the log.

aprende.t: What a log line needs to have
The observado() wrapper on the three doors
Error, refusal, cancellation, and the MRTR request
Why the log keeps the field name and not the value

hero_alt: Dark monitor with unreadable log lines and a timeline, next to an open notebook and a pen.

secoes.titulo: From the request to the line in the log
secoes.sub: The log sits at the boundary, not inside the rule. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: Form (html), executeTool on the page (webmcp), or tools/call on the server (mcp).
observado(superficie, ferramenta, fn) measures the time, classifies the result, and returns the response unchanged. It lives in pagina/registro.mjs and serves all three doors.
ok · erro (the rule refused) · recusado (the person said no) · cancelado (AbortSignal) · pediu-pessoa (MRTR 1st round) · excecao.
One line per call: t, superficie, ferramenta, campos, resultado, ms, and motivo. The campos are only the NAMES of the input.
How many of each outcome, per surface. This is where the right question comes from: does the agent get the input wrong, or does the person refuse?

secoes.sub: Each one calls for a different action from whoever runs the site.

texto: Input that the rule does not accept: invalid topic, workshop with no spots left.
Many errors on the same tool = a confusing description or schema for the agent.
The confirmation worked. It is not a site failure.
Many refusals = the agent is proposing the wrong thing; look at what it asked for.
The agent gave up (or the person left) before the response: executeTool was canceled by the signal.
Measured in the kit: the cancellation reaches execute as AbortError and the booking does not happen.
In MCP 2026-07-28, the first round of an action with confirmation returns input_required.
That is why a booking through MCP leaves two lines: the request and the outcome.

secoes.sub: The same file serves the page and the server. On the page, in production, the line would go to your backend (sendBeacon, for example); in the kit it stays in memory.

secoes.titulo: Trigger the outcomes and read the log
secoes.sub: The script searches, gets the topic wrong, refuses, cancels, and books through MCP with a refusal. It writes logs/chamadas.jsonl.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-expert-v72/kit
node scripts/observar.mjs nativo; echo "saída: $?"
tail -1 logs/chamadas.jsonl

abas.html:
== Chromium 156.0.8078.4 (Playwright) · modo: nativo
html   buscar_oficinas  ok              0 ms
webmcp buscar_oficinas  ok              0 ms
webmcp buscar_oficinas  erro            3 ms · tema inválido: cobol
webmcp reservar_vaga    recusado      184 ms
webmcp reservar_vaga    cancelado     319 ms · AbortError
mcp    buscar_oficinas  ok              0 ms
mcp    reservar_vaga    pediu-pessoa   26 ms
mcp    reservar_vaga    recusado        2 ms
REGISTRO: 8 chamadas · ok 3 · erro 1 · recusado 2 · cancelado 1 · pediu-pessoa 1 · dado pessoal no registro: não
gravado em logs/chamadas.jsonl
saída: 0
{"t":"2026-10-19T20:03:13.159Z","superficie":"mcp","ferramenta":"reservar_vaga","campos":["id","nome"],"resultado":"recusado","ms":2}

The last line is a real line from the file: the fields id and nome show up by name, never by value. The milliseconds vary on each run.

abas.rot: Common mistake: logging the whole input
abas.html:
REGISTRO: 8 chamadas · ok 3 · erro 1 · recusado 2 · cancelado 1 · pediu-pessoa 1 · dado pessoal no registro: SIM
saída: 1

Someone swapped campos for entrada: input "to debug". People's names ended up in the log, and the script exits with 1. A log with personal data becomes a liability (LGPD): log what helps you operate, not what identifies someone.

secoes.sub: On a throwaway copy of the kit.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos/formacao-webmcp-expert-v72/kit
E=$(bash scripts/copia.sh a3)
# o erro comum: registrar a entrada inteira "para depurar"
sed -i 's/campos: Object.keys(input).sort()/entrada: input/' $E/pagina/registro.mjs
cd $E && node scripts/observar.mjs nativo | grep "REGISTRO"; echo "saída: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

secoes.sub: Read the log, watch the leak get caught, and decide what your site logs. Each exercise ends in a done when.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · The outcomes in the log
exercicios.texto: Run the logging block and count the lines by outcome.
exercicios.pronto: node scripts/observar.mjs nativo; echo "saída: $?" → REGISTRO: 8 chamadas · ok 3 · erro 1 · recusado 2 · cancelado 1 · pediu-pessoa 1 · dado pessoal no registro: não and saída: 0.

exercicios.texto: Run the log rehearsal with the whole input.
exercicios.pronto: The block prints dado pessoal no registro: SIM and saída: 1.

exercicios.texto: For your site's tools, write which fields go into the log (name only), where the line goes in production, and who looks at the summary each week.
exercicios.pronto: The file registro-[your site].md has one line per tool, the log destination, and the owner, and no field with an input value.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after the answer.

perguntas.p: The MCP booking with confirmation left two lines in the log. Why?
opcoes: The MCP client repeated the call on its own because of a network error.
The SDK logs every call twice for safety.
The server kept a session and reopened it on the second line.
The 1st round asks for the person (input_required); the 2nd brings the outcome.
perguntas.explica: This is the MRTR from the 2026-07-28 revision: the tool returns input_required, the client asks, and the call is repeated. There is no session in the protocol.

perguntas.p: The log shows many "recusado" lines in reservar_vaga. What should you look at first?
opcoes: What the agent proposed: the confirmation is working.
The server, because a refusal means it went down.
The schema, because a refusal is invalid input.
The browser, because a refusal means the API is missing.
perguntas.explica: Recusado = the person said no. The protection worked; many refusals suggest the agent is proposing the wrong thing. Invalid input shows up as an error.

perguntas.p: Why does the log store campos: ["id", "nome"] and not the values?
opcoes: Because executeTool does not hand the values to execute.
To operate without keeping personal data about who booked.
Because JSONL does not accept text with accents.
To keep the log smaller so the disk does not fill up.
perguntas.explica: The name of the person booking is personal data. To operate, all you need to know is that the call had an id and a name, the outcome, and the time. The rehearsal shows the script catching the leak.

perguntas.p: Where does the observado() wrapper live in the kit?
opcoes: Inside oficinas.mjs, so the rule registers itself.
Only in the MCP server, because the page has nowhere to write.
At the boundary of each door, around execute.
In Chromium, which logs the WebMCP calls.
perguntas.explica: The log sits at the boundary (form, WebMCP tool, MCP tool), around execute. The rule stays pure and the same registro.mjs serves the page and the server.

itens.texto: Surface, tool, field names, outcome, and time: one per call.
Error, refusal, cancellation, and an MRTR request tell different stories.
The input value stays out of the log; the script catches whoever forgets.
